prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofing company for every homeowner — the right choice depends on your goals (lowest price, best warranty, fastest timeline, experience with insurance claims, etc.). If you tell me your ZIP code and what matters most to you, I can recommend a short list of top-rated roofers in your area. Meanwhile, here’s a practical way to find the best Dallas roofing company for your replacement and a few things to watch for.

How to pick the best roofer for you
- Prioritize what matters: price, long workmanship warranty, manufacturer-certified installers, insurance-claim experience, or fast scheduling.
- Get at least 3 written estimates for the exact same scope of work and materials so you can compare apples-to-apples.
- Verify insurance and licensing: ask for proof of liability insurance and workers’ comp (or a waiver if subcontractors are used). Confirm they’re a local company with a Dallas address or local office.
- Check reputation: Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi, and the BBB. Look for recent projects and photos.
- Prefer manufacturer-certified contractors (GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed Select, etc.) for better product warranties.
- Ask about warranties: manufacturer warranty on shingles and a separate workmanship warranty from the contractor (get both in writing).
- Confirm permit and inspection handling — the contractor should pull local permits and arrange final inspections.
- Beware storm chasers: after storms, some out-of-area companies canvass neighborhoods; prefer established local businesses and check references.
- Check sample contract: scope of work, materials by brand and color, payment schedule, start and completion dates, cleanup, and lien releases.

Key questions to ask any roofer
1. How long have you been in business in the Dallas area?  
2. Can you provide local references and recent project photos?  
3. Are you manufacturer-certified (GAF, OC, CertainTeed, etc.)? Which ones?  
4. Can you show proof of liability insurance and workers’ comp?  
5. Will you pull the permits and arrange inspections?  
6. What warranties do you offer (materials and workmanship) and are they written?  
7. What is the estimated timeline and payment schedule?  
8. Who will perform the work — your employees or subs?  
9. How will you handle storm-damage/insurance claims (if applicable)?  
10. Do you provide a lien waiver upon final payment?

Red flags
- High-pressure sales tactics or “limited-time” storm-only pricing.  
- No proof of insurance or unwillingness to provide references.  
- Demands for large upfront cash payment (reasonable deposit is normal, but protect yourself).  
- Vague or no written contract and unclear warranty terms.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated roofing contractors in Dallas (give me your ZIP or neighborhood), or  
- Review estimates or contractor bids you already have and help compare them line-by-line.

Which would you prefer?
